newsitem.title: QATAR: Ministers hope Bahrain will attend Gulf Arab summit.
newsitem.headline: Ministers hope Bahrain will attend Gulf Arab summit.

text.p: Gulf Arab foreign ministers said on Sunday the participation of their fellow partner Bahrain in a summit in December was important and expressed hopes Manama would reverse a decision to boycott the meeting.

"There was a strong opinion that Bahrain should revise its decision and come to the summit," Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani told reporters at the end of a two-day meeting of the foreign ministers of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).
"Qatar is ready to do its best to welcome Bahrain to the summit. Participation of Bahrain is very important. We hope they will come," he added.
He said GCC Secretary-General Jameel al-Hujailan will hold talks in Bahrain -- which is locked in a territorial dispute with Qatar -- in the next few days.
Sheikh Hamad said the ministers "nearly finalised the agenda" for the December 7-9 summit of the leaders of the GCC -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Bahrain.

Bahrain has boycotted the foreign ministers' meeting in Doha and has threatened to boycott the summit unless Doha withdrew a case it had taken to the International Court of Justice at The Hague over a number of barren islands, sandbanks and reefs controlled by Bahrain but also claimed by Qatar.
Qatar has said it would only withdraw the case if Saudi Arabia's mediation to resolve the dispute succeeded.
